body:
"V1.3 Sanitization and Sandboxing"

Only 2 requirements mention "sandboxing", but it is not clear for me - is it some historical reason or there is actual reason and content for that?
* V1.3.2 Verify that the application avoids the use of eval() or other dynamic code execution features such as Spring Expression Language (SpEL). Where there is no alternative, any user input being included must be sanitized or **sandboxed** before being executed.
* V1.3.5 Verify that the application sanitizes, disables, or **sandboxes** user-supplied scriptable or expression template language content, such as Markdown, CSS or XSL stylesheets, BBCode, or similar.

What was the idea behind SVG requirement cleanup - requirement 1.3.4 only says, that sanitize the input to the version that is safe for the application. Sandboxing comes into play when the content is used.

For server-side we have sandboxing mentioned in V15.2 section
* V15.2.4 Verify that the application implements additional protections around parts of the application which are documented as performing "risky" operations or using "risky" third-party libraries. This could include techniques such as **sandboxing**, encapsulation, containerization or network level isolation to delay and deter attackers who compromise one part of an application from pivoting elsewhere in the application.

comments.body:
I think 1.3.2 just looks strange, I think it can go away. I am not sure the historical reason for it. Plus it's a negative requirement.

1.3.5 seems like a catch-all way to handle input from the user that needs to be executed in some way. Since we have matured so many requirements around this (HTML Sanitization 1.3.1, SVG requirements 1.3.4, CSS 1.2.1 and similar) I think this is a candidate to go away as well.

V15.2.4 seems legit, but I think it should be matured. If we really want to talk sandboxing, I would discuss the iframe sandbox attribute or isolating pages into different origins on the same page (and then use web messaging to communicate between sandboxed frames) which seem to be more mature and standard browser sandboxes. This is what I see dropbox and other security-centric sites doing.

I don't think V1.3.2 or V1.3.5 should go away entirely, I only question the "sandbox" part in those requirements.

V15.2.4 is given just an example that we have sandboxing handled for the server-side. iframe sanboxing does not belong into this topic.

for client-side sandboxing we have:
> V3.2.1 Verify that security controls are in place to prevent browsers from rendering content or functionality in HTTP responses in an incorrect context (e.g., when an API, a user-uploaded file or other resource is requested directly). Possible controls could include: not serving the content unless HTTP request header fields (such as Sec-Fetch-*) indicate it is the correct context, using the **sandbox** directive of the Content-Security-Policy header field or using the attachment disposition type in the Content-Disposition header field.

What comes to iframes and web messages, I feel that is a bit offtopic from here.

title: V1.3 review - is sandboxing a deprecated topic for this
